\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عرس} (ʿurs)}{عرس (ʿurs)}]{\ar{عرس} (ʿurs) — a wedding feast, a wedding}

\label{lesson:AR-C306-urs}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a defendant, then the Arabic for to pass judgment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عرس}}
\textbf{\ar{عرس}} — \emph{ʿurs} — \textquotedblleft{}a wedding feast, a wedding\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حضرنا} \ar{عرس} \ar{ابن} \ar{عمي} \ar{في} \ar{القرية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaḍarnā ʿurs ibn ʿammī fī al-qarya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We went to my cousin’s wedding in the village.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أعراس}, \emph{aʿrās}.

The taught \ar{عروس}, bride, and \ar{عريس}, groom, are the same root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عرس}} (\emph{ʿurs}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-r-s} (Lane), the root of the taught \emph{ʿarūs}, a bride, and \emph{ʿarīs}, a groom. \emph{ʿUrs} is the feast held for them.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿurs}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿurs}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaḍarnā ʿurs ibn ʿammī fī al-qarya.} — We went to my cousin’s wedding in the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a defendant, then the Arabic for to pass judgment, then say \emph{ʿurs} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عرس} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wedding feast, a wedding\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{خطب} (khaṭaba)}{خطب (khaṭaba)}]{\ar{خطب} (khaṭaba) — to propose marriage; to make a speech}

\label{lesson:AR-C306-khataba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to pass judgment, then the Arabic for a wedding feast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خطب}}
\textbf{\ar{خطب}} — \emph{khaṭaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to propose marriage; to make a speech\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{خطب} \ar{أخي} \ar{جارتنا} \ar{الشهر} \ar{الماضي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khaṭaba akhī jāratanā ash-shahr al-māḍī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother asked our neighbour to marry him last month.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يخطب}, \emph{yakhṭub}.

\ar{خطب} \ar{فتاة}: to ask for her hand. \ar{خطب} \ar{في} \ar{الناس}: to speak to a crowd.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{خطب}} (\emph{khaṭaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-ṭ-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to address, to speak to\textquotedblright{}. Lane gives both senses: \emph{khiṭba}, asking for a woman in marriage, and \emph{khuṭba}, a speech.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khaṭaba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khaṭaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khaṭaba akhī jāratanā ash-shahr al-māḍī.} — My brother asked our neighbour to marry him last month.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to pass judgment, then the Arabic for a wedding feast, then say \emph{khaṭaba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{خطب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To propose marriage; to make a speech\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{خطوبة} (khuṭūba)}{خطوبة (khuṭūba)}]{\ar{خطوبة} (khuṭūba) — an engagement to marry}

\label{lesson:AR-C306-khutuba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a wedding feast, then the Arabic for to propose marriage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خطوبة}}
\textbf{\ar{خطوبة}} — \emph{khuṭūba} — \textquotedblleft{}an engagement to marry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أعلنت} \ar{أختي} \ar{خطوبتها} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aʿlanat ukhtī khuṭūbatahā ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister announced her engagement yesterday.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{خطوبة}} (\emph{khuṭūba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-ṭ-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to address; to ask in marriage\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Khuṭūba} is the time between the asking and the wedding.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khuṭūba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khuṭūba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aʿlanat ukhtī khuṭūbatahā ams.} — My sister announced her engagement yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a wedding feast, then the Arabic for to propose marriage, then say \emph{khuṭūba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{خطوبة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An engagement to marry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{زف} (zaffa)}{زف (zaffa)}]{\ar{زف} (zaffa) — to escort a bride; to bring good news}

\label{lesson:AR-C306-zaffa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to propose marriage, then the Arabic for an engagement to marry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{زف}}
\textbf{\ar{زف}} — \emph{zaffa} — \textquotedblleft{}to escort a bride; to bring good news\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{زف} \ar{الأهل} \ar{العروس} \ar{إلى} \ar{بيتها} \ar{الجديد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zaffa al-ahl al-ʿarūs ilā baytihā al-jadīd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The family led the bride to her new home.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يزف}, \emph{yazuff}.

The taught \ar{زفاف}, a wedding, is its verbal noun. \ar{زف} \ar{إليه} \ar{الخبر}: he brought him the good news.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{زف}} (\emph{zaffa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{z-f-f} (Lane), where \emph{zaffa al-ʿarūs} is to conduct the bride to her husband with music and pageantry; \emph{zifāf} is its verbal noun.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaffa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaffa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaffa al-ahl al-ʿarūs ilā baytihā al-jadīd.} — The family led the bride to her new home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to propose marriage, then the Arabic for an engagement to marry, then say \emph{zaffa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{زغرد} (zaghrada)}{زغرد (zaghrada)}]{\ar{زغرد} (zaghrada) — to ululate for joy}

\label{lesson:AR-C306-zaghrada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an engagement to marry, then the Arabic for to escort a bride.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{زغرد}}
\textbf{\ar{زغرد}} — \emph{zaghrada} — \textquotedblleft{}to ululate for joy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{زغردت} \ar{النساء} \ar{عندما} \ar{دخلت} \ar{العروس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zaghradat an-nisāʾ ʿindamā dakhalat al-ʿarūs.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The women ululated when the bride came in.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يزغرد}, \emph{yuzaghrid}.

The cry itself is \ar{زغرودة}; plural \ar{زغاريد}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{زغرد}} (\emph{zaghrada}) is built on the native Arabic four-letter root \emph{z-gh-r-d} (Lane), first said of the bray a camel rolls in its throat, then of the trilling cry women raise at a wedding.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaghrada}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaghrada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaghradat an-nisāʾ ʿindamā dakhalat al-ʿarūs.} — The women ululated when the bride came in.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an engagement to marry, then the Arabic for to escort a bride, then say \emph{zaghrada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{زغرد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To ululate for joy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
